reviews.text:
Was awesome, quality has dipped.. This app used to be amazing, but a problem that has existed for a while and a recent issue have cause the quality to lessen.

The most recent issue, is that the speed of the painting being created is now sluggishly slow. Whereas previously it would paint at a speed that was much faster and reasonable.

And the issue that has persisted for a while is, that there’ll be white splotches or tiny white marks present in the painting often, even when no ounce of white exists in that specific area of the the picture. And so it leaves this rough, unfinished quality to the painting, which ruins an otherwise amazing painting. And letting it continue to paint tends to target other things.

I really hope they can try to fix these issues, because I can’t devote so much time sitting around waiting for these paintings to generate with it moving as slow as it does and with all the blemishes that make them seem incomplete.

An Incredible Art Tool. The effects you can build with Oilist are just mind-blowing in my opinion. I have taken some paintings that I created and was pretty proud of and turned them into something truly amazing with this program.

I should say, too, that I usually don't have any interest in apps that will supposedly turn your photos and images into regular paintings or oil paintings. I always found the notion of that concept and genre just silly. But, I'm glad I took a chance with this one because to me it is really different and stands out from the crowd in what it allows you to create.

Plus, I really like the aspect of the app on how it is constantly working to create effects in your photos and keeps generating new looks the entire time you're using it. Definitely a one-of-a-kind application in my opinion and well worth the decent asking price. Thanks for creating this app, its continued support and God bless.

reviews.text:
Worth the Time to Create Masterpieces!. I am glad that I waited 8 months before writing a review, because I might have agreed with some of the lower-rated reviews when I began. But, I now find that this app is magnificent! I don't read manuals, preferring to learn while experimenting with an app until I get the results I'm happy with. If you start off expecting Oilist to match the examples in 15 seconds, you'll be disappointed. As a former real-world painter who spent months on a painting, I eventually decided to let the app do its thing and come back to it later. It did a great job on the default settings, matching the examples, but I decided to play with the options to see what I could do. Some things worked, others didn't, just as experimenting did with oils and acrylics. To my joy, I went on to to win an award for an Oilist painting I submitted in a digital art show. I have 3 suggestions for dissatisfied users, and one request for the developer for future improvements.
1. TECHNICALLY, You will get the best results from your largest resolution images, with good composition, areas of light and dark, and great contrast (unless you want soft/impressionist-like results). 
2. INVEST THE TIME to allow the app to fully resolve the style you choose, make sure you choose higher 'density' so any specks of "canvas" will cover more quickly, and adjust back to suit your needs, THEN make adjustments, and experiment. If you want fast ho-hum results, there are 10+ apps that'll do it for you. I use a few, but nothing comes close to Oilist.
3. FREE YOURSELF FROM EXPECTATION, and let yourself make mistakes, see how Oiliest resolves them. My best work seems to arise from surprising results/accidents and the intuitive ways Oilist responds, and if you don't like the results, try an adjustment!

To the developer--While I'd love an 'erase' & 'redo' tool for small areas, I'd be happiest with a masking tool that can be introduced at any stage of the painting process. 

And to anyone reading to the bottom here, I was not paid or asked by the app to write anything here, and as a harsh critic of many apps I've reviewed, I stand by everything above! It's a rare 5 star review for me!

reviews.text: Spectacular results!. This app allows you to create fantastic and unique digital art. Patience while the app continuously "paints" will result in spectacular results. The app also creates high resolution images so you can have prints made without fear of pixelation. I would love to see the ability to add a digital signature directly to my art but even without that feature I would highly recommend this to anyone who enjoys converting photos into fantabulous digital art. An absolute steal at $2.99, WORTH EVERY PENNY!

reviews.text: Relaxing and satisfying. This app is pretty nice. The instructions are quite clear and it operates exactly as advertised. It only takes a moment to start taking shape. The longer you let it roll, the more detail and style it will incorporate. Mid-painting snapshots are a nice idea and linking to a printable canvas service is convenient. Worth the money if you're looking for an easy yet sophisticated oil painting processor.

reviews.text: A bit disappointed. I find the images to be unusable because there are either white spots of unused space, or when everything is colored in, the "painting" feels like a blurry painting of the original image ... I tried all the styles with a simple photo of a baby, and many times the styles would make her look like had the measles or mumps and make bumpy changes in the skin... I will definitely await updates and look forward to improvements ... I think you could have the app be $1 for three styles and then an IAP for access to other styles... also, perhaps styles could be named after impressionist painters? That would be easier to understand than try each on... also would like to have a simple finished painting option rather than watch the painting unfold, I don't want images with blank spaces . Thanks

reviews.text: The photo painting app I've been waiting for. I've often used painting apps and been unhappy with all results. Prisma is solid, waterlogue is great too, but Oilist gives complete control. It continuously paints while you make adjustments to brush size, type, density, direction and added chaos (spin, zoom, explode and noise). I haven't had this much fun editing a photo in a long time.
